MYP Arts is assessed on four criteria, each out of 8: **A Investigating**, **B Developing**, **C Creating/Performing** and **D Evaluating**.
This lesson is about B: how you get from an idea to the piece you will make or perform. It is shown almost entirely through your
[process journal](process-journal.qmd).

The wording below is from the IB's *Arts guide* for use from September 2022, Year 5 (the last year of the MYP). Years 1 and 3 have their own,
simpler wording. Ask your teacher for the version for your year.

## 1. What Criterion B asks

At the end of Year 5, students should be able to:

> i. practically explore ideas to inform development of a final artwork or performance
>
> ii. present a clear artistic intention for the final artwork or performance in line with the statement of inquiry.

That is two things: **exploring in practice**, and **saying what you intend and why**.

## 2. Strand i: practical exploration

*Practical* means in sound, with your instrument, voice, software or players, not only thinking about it. *Explore* means trying more than one
possibility before choosing. The levels go from *limited*, through *sufficient* and *substantial*, to *extensive and varied* practical exploration.

**Extensive** means a lot of it. **Varied** means different kinds. Ten versions of the same melody with one note changed is a lot, but it isn't varied.
Ways to explore in music:

| Explore | For example |
|---|---|
| **Material** | three different motifs for the opening; three chord progressions under the same melody |
| **Development** | the motif in sequence, inversion, augmentation (try them in the [motif lab](compose-motif.qmd#the-motif-lab)) |
| **Form** | verse–chorus or AABA; where the climax goes; how it ends |
| **Sound** | which instrument plays the tune; doubling; register; a synth patch or an effect |
| **Performance** | tempo, dynamics, articulation, phrasing: record it three ways and compare |
| **Testing** | a player tries your part; a friend hears two versions without being told which is which |

Each one counts as exploration in your journal only with **evidence** (the recordings, scores or screenshots of each version) and a line on
**what you found out**.

<div class="cp-tip">
<strong>Explore before you settle.</strong> If your first idea is in the final piece unchanged, there is little exploration to show, however good
the idea is. Try alternatives even when you like the first one. Keeping it after a fair comparison is a decision you can explain.
</div>

## 3. Strand ii: the artistic intention

An **artistic intention** says what you are going to make or perform and what you want it to do, and it connects to your unit's **statement of
inquiry** (the big idea your teacher gives the unit). In the Year 5 descriptors, every level asks for a *clear artistic intention in line with the
statement of inquiry*. What changes from level to level is what you do with your **artistic choices**:

| Level | The student presents a clear artistic intention ... and |
|---|---|
| 1–2 | **states** artistic choices |
| 3–4 | **describes** artistic choices |
| 5–6 | **explains** artistic choices |
| 7–8 | **justifies** artistic choices |

These are **command terms**, and the IB defines each one:

- **State:** give a specific name, value or other brief answer without explanation or calculation.
- **Describe:** give a detailed account or picture of a situation, event, pattern or process.
- **Explain:** give a detailed account including reasons or causes.
- **Justify:** give valid reasons or evidence to support an answer or conclusion.

In practice: *state* names the choice. *Describe* adds the musical detail. *Explain* adds the reason. *Justify* backs the reason with evidence:
a piece you studied, a test you recorded, feedback you got.

### Try it: which is which?

Four sentences about the same choice. Match each to its command term.

<div class="cp-try">
<div class="cp-sort"></div>
</div>

## 4. Build your intention

Fill in the boxes. The intention is written as you type, and kept in this browser. Under it is a rough guide to how far your choices go,
from *state* to *justify*. It only counts words, though: it can't judge whether your reasons are good. Your teacher can.

<div class="cp-try">
<div class="cp-intent"></div>
</div>

## 5. A worked example

A Year 5 unit with the statement of inquiry *"Composers use repetition and contrast to shape a listener's experience over time."*

> **Intention.** I intend to make a 24-bar piano piece in ABA form for the class recital, so that the listener feels settled, then unsettled, then
> settled again but changed. **Choices.** The A section uses a four-note motif in a period, in C major, mostly steps, *mp*, because steps and
> repeated rhythm sound settled. I tested this: in `A_v1` the melody leapt a lot and two classmates called it "restless"; in `A_v3`, mostly
> steps, they called it "calm". The B section develops the same motif by inversion and sequence, in A minor, *f*, because I want the contrast
> to come from the same idea. In Beethoven's Fifth (first movement) the opening motif returns throughout in changed forms, and I wanted that
> unity. The return of A is in augmentation so it sounds familiar but slower and further on.

This intention is clear, connected to the statement of inquiry, and its choices come with reasons and evidence (tests and a piece studied). That
evidence is in the journal: `A_v1` and `A_v3`, the classmates' comments, the score of B with the inversions labelled.

## 6. For teachers

- These strands, descriptors and command terms are from the Year 5 criteria of the *Arts guide* (for use from September 2022/January 2023), read
  from a school's published copy. Years 1 and 3 differ in wording.
- The earlier *Arts guide*, which this one replaced, has a Criterion B called *Developing skills*, about acquiring and applying skills and techniques; its
  Criterion C, *Thinking creatively*, held the artistic intention and the exploration of ideas. Students' older exemplars and school documents
  may still use that wording.
- The composing lessons give B-friendly tasks: the [motif lab](compose-motif.qmd#the-motif-lab) (explore by development), the takes in
  [Composing 3](compose-song.qmd#write-a-verse-and-a-chorus) (explore by performance), and the two quartet textures in
  [Composing 5](compose-orchestra.qmd#the-same-melody-two-ways) (a choice to explain).
